toast.createdDomainFailed: Application created, but the domain could not be added: {error}
toast.hostPortRolling: Host port saved; applied through a configuration deployment (see History).
toast.hostPortOnStart: Host port saved; takes effect when the application is started again.
toast.applyingHostPort: Applying host port — recreating the container…

git.title: Git repo (built)
git.description: Clone the repo, build an image, then run it.

image.title: Ready-made image (pulled)
image.description: Pull an image from a registry, no build.

image.title: Image
image.label: Image
image.description: Pulled again on every deploy, so moving tags such as latest stay up to date. No build and no local registry.
image.autoUpdateSwitch: Redeploy when the tag's digest changes in the registry
image.autoUpdateHelp: Like Watchtower: the manifest digest is compared through the registry API (Docker Hub, GHCR, local registry), without pulling. Tags pinned by digest (@sha256:…) never change.

git.title: Git repository
git.label: Git repository
git.description: A git repo that can be cloned over HTTPS.
git.rootDirectoryHelp: For monorepos: the folder that is built, e.g. apps/web. The Dockerfile path and output folder below are relative to this folder, and files outside it are not part of the build.
git.watchRootAria: Deploy only when this folder changes
git.watchRoot: Webhook: deploy only when files in this folder change
git.railpackHelp: Railpack (Railway) also detects the stack from the repo contents, but its build runs on BuildKit so dependency cache persists between deploys (tested here: 284 s54 s). Needs a BuildKit container on the host — started automatically on the first build; applications on a remote server are not supported. Build args are passed as --env.
git.nixpacksHelp: Nixpacks recognizes Node, Python, Go, PHP, Ruby, Rust and more from the repo contents. The first build is slower (base image ±430 MB + package installation through Nix); the build cache is disabled — use Railpack if you want a cache. The build args below are passed to Nixpacks as env (e.g. NIXPACKS_NODE_VERSION=22).
git.credentialHelp: For private repos; add a credential in Integrations → Git credentials.

static.buildCommandPlaceholder: npm ci && npm run build (empty = files are already in the repo)
static.buildCommandHelp: Runs in the node:22-alpine image; the result is copied to nginx. Leave empty for plain static HTML.
static.spaHelp: Container port = 80. Turn on for React/Vue Router.

network.title: Network & access
network.staticNote: Static sites are served by nginx on port 80.
network.applyRecreate: Applied immediately: the container is recreated from the running image (no build; brief downtime because two containers cannot use the same port).
network.applyRolling: Applied as a configuration deployment (swarm service rolling update).
network.applyOnStart: The application is stopped: takes effect when it is started again.
network.applyNextDeploy: Takes effect on the first deploy.
network.healthcheckHelp: The deploy waits for this path to answer 2xx/3xx inside the container (needs wget/curl/node/python3 in the image). For apps routed through a domain without a host port, the new container is started beside the old one and only replaces it once healthy — no downtime. If it never becomes healthy the deploy fails and the old container keeps running.

access.label: Access
access.description: Without a host port or domain, the application runs but cannot be opened from outside — you can also set this later in the Settings or Domain tab.
access.hostPortHelp: Opened directly through the IP: {url}, without a domain/proxy.
access.domainHelp: Opened through the reverse proxy (point this host's DNS to this server).
access.proxyNotRunning: The proxy is not running — it will be started automatically if needed.
access.httpsNeedsAcme: HTTPS requires PROXY_ACME_EMAIL on the API.
access.laterHelp: The application is created without an access address — set a host port or domain later.

env.label: Environment variables
env.description: Applied on the next deploy, on top of the linked variable sets.

advanced.title: Resources & advanced
advanced.serverHelp: On a remote server: the build and the container run on that server's Docker (over SSH) and the image is not pushed to the registry. Domains are served by that server's own proxy (Infrastructure<arrow></arrow>Remote servers<arrow></arrow>Proxy).
advanced.modeService: Swarm service (replicas, rolling update by the daemon)
advanced.deployModeHelp: A service runs on the aoox host only. Stop/start = scale to 0 and back; logs & metrics come from its tasks. Changing the mode = redeploy the last image. Replicas > 1 share the same volume mounts.
advanced.constraintHelp: Node labels are set in Settings<arrow></arrow>Docker Swarm. Combined with the placement below (all must be satisfied).
advanced.orderAuto: Automatic (start-first; stop-first when there is a host port)
advanced.placementHelp: Applications with mounts are always placed on the aoox host (their volumes live there). Tasks on other nodes: logs still show, but job exec & metrics only work for tasks on the host.
advanced.memoryHelp: Applied immediately to the running container (removing a limit = the container is recreated).
advanced.deploymentKeepHelp: Number of successful deployments (with their images) kept for rollback; older ones are deleted during the nightly cleanup.
advanced.ignoreErrorsHelp: Skip this application in the automatic log scan (the Application error notification) — for applications whose normal output looks like errors.
advanced.buildArgsHelp: One KEY=VALUE per line, passed to ARG in the Dockerfile at build time. They are stored in the image — do not use for secrets; references are not supported.

previews.label: Pull request previews
previews.switch: Build & run every opened PR (via webhook)
previews.domainPlaceholder: preview.example.com (optional; defaults to the API's PREVIEW_DOMAIN)
previews.help: Previews are reachable at ''-pr''.'' (needs wildcard DNS to this host). PRs from forks are always ignored — a PR branch is arbitrary code. At most 5 open previews per application. Enable the Pull requests event in the provider's webhook.

variableSets.title: Variable sets
variableSets.description: Optional: link environments of shared variable sets. More can be linked, reordered or removed later on the Environment tab.

page.newDescription: Built from a git repo (Dockerfile, Nixpacks, or static site) or pulled from a ready-made image, then run as a container.

tabs.settingsDescription: Host port, domains, and resource limits are applied directly to the running application; other settings take effect on the next deploy.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: This application's env variables. Applied on the next deploy (values are read when the container is created), on top of the linked variable sets: on the same key, this one wins.
environment.readOnly: Only developers and above can change the environment.

imagePicker.title: Choose an image from a registry
imagePicker.description: Only shows repositories/tags that have already been pushed — run docker push first if there are none.
imagePicker.noImages: No images in this registry yet

delete.title: Delete application?
delete.description: The container {name} will be stopped and removed. Images in the registry are not deleted.

validation.rootDirectoryFormat: Relative folder, e.g. apps/web (no .. and no leading /)
validation.staticOutputDir: Folder relative to the repo root
validation.gitUrlFormat: Must be an http(s) or git:// URL

shared.envRefsWithDb: Values can reference {varsRef} and this project's databases: (also .host, .port, .username, .password, .database).

proxyWarning.title: Reverse proxy was not running — it has been started automatically
proxyWarning.intro: The proxy (Traefik) was not running before this domain was saved, so it was started automatically. The new domain is reachable once these three things are also in place:
proxyWarning.dns: The domain's DNS points to this server's IP.
proxyWarning.ports: Ports 80 and 443 are open to the public (OS firewall and VPS provider).
proxyWarning.cert: The HTTPS certificate (Let's Encrypt) is only issued the first time the domain is visited — wait a minute.

noAccess.title: This application has no access address
noAccess.body: Without a host port or a domain, this application can only be reached inside the Docker network.

image.pinned: The reference uses a fixed digest — nothing changed.
image.baseline: Digest recorded ({digest}); nothing to compare yet.
image.changedBusy: Image changed ({digest}) — another deployment is running.

logs.connectFailed: Could not connect to the logs

origin.title: Realtime logs are not available at this address
origin.body: This panel has a custom domain ({webOrigin}), and realtime logs only accept connections from that domain — not from {browserOrigin}, which you are using now.

history.emptyBody: Deploy your app to see its build history here.

section.title: Deployments
section.description: {count, plural, =0 {Never deployed} one {# deployment} other {# deployments}} · Select one to read its log.

proxyStopped.title: Proxy is not running
proxyStopped.body: New domains take effect once the reverse proxy is enabled on the Settings page.

domains.notDeployed: Domains are applied to the container when the application is deployed.

autoProvisioned.title: Reverse proxy was not running — it has been started automatically
autoProvisioned.intro: The proxy (Traefik) was not running before this, so it was started automatically for the domain {host}. Check these one by one if the domain is still unreachable after a few minutes:
autoProvisioned.dns: The DNS A record for {host} points to this server's IP.
autoProvisioned.ports: Ports 80 and 443 are open to the public — both the OS firewall (ufw) and your VPS/server provider's firewall or security group.
autoProvisioned.cert: If you asked for HTTPS: the certificate (Let's Encrypt) is only issued by Traefik the first time the domain is visited, which takes a few seconds to a minute — and only if the ACME email is set (host: panel Domain; remote server: server settings).

domains.empty: No domains yet. The application can only be reached through its host port.

dns.detected: Public IP detected automatically; set PUBLIC_IP on the API if it is wrong.

expiry.daysLeft: {days, plural, one {# day left} other {# days left}}

section.title: Domains
section.description: {count, plural, =0 {No domains yet} one {# domain} other {# domains}} · Each host is routed to this application by the reverse proxy.

add.title: Add domain
add.description: Route a hostname to this application through the reverse proxy.

conflict.orphan: Container {name} was left over from a deleted project or app and still answers on this domain, so requests are split between it and this app. Remove it in the Docker page (Details).
conflict.other: Container {name} also routes this domain, so requests are split between it and this app. Stop or remove it, or use another hostname.

middlewares.title: Middleware for {host}
middlewares.description: Run in the order they are selected, before the request reaches the application. Saving recreates the container without a build. HTTP-only and HTTPS domains both use them; the http→https redirect does not.
middlewares.empty: No middleware yet. The owner creates them under Infrastructure → Reverse proxy → Dynamic configuration.

new.title: New job
new.description: The command is run with sh -c. In the container: docker exec in the running container (e.g. {example}). Separate container: a one-off container from the same image{extra} — for heavy work or when the container is stopped. A job that is still running is not started twice.

extra.application: with the application's env and mounts

row.deleteDescription: The job is permanently deleted along with its run history, and its schedule stops. This cannot be undone.

section.title: Jobs
section.description: {count, plural, =0 {No jobs yet} one {# job} other {# jobs}} · Run a command on a schedule or on demand.

monitor.title: HTTP monitor
monitor.description: Checks the application over HTTP periodically and sends a notification after several failures in a row. An application whose container is alive but returns 5xx or hangs is caught here.

target.label: Target (derived from the application, cannot be changed)
target.note: The check runs from the panel machine: it does not prove the application is reachable from the outside internet. With a public domain, the result can be affected by hairpin NAT.

fields.useInternal: Check through the internal address (skip the public domain)

series.empty: No data yet — the first check runs within a minute.
series.aria: Latency over the last 24 hours, latest {value} ms

add.title: Add mount
add.description: Volume: persistent data that survives deploys (a named Docker volume). Bind: a folder/file on the host (owner/admin only). File: a small config file stored here and mounted read-only. Changes are applied immediately by recreating the container{suffix}.
add.suffixDatabase: (brief restart; data stays in the volume)

row.detachVolumeDescription: The mount is detached from the container. Choose what happens to its Docker volume: keep it (data stays) or delete it too (data is lost permanently and cannot be recovered).
row.detachDescription: The mount is detached from the container. This cannot be undone.

section.title: Mounts
section.description: {count, plural, =0 {No mounts yet} one {# mount} other {# mounts}} · A change recreates the container; data in volumes is kept.

secretSource.title: Secret source
secretSource.description: Pull secrets from a secret manager (Infisical) instead of copying them into the env. Values are fetched when the container is created (deploy, apply config, rollback); reference a single secret with {ref} in the env, or turn on Sync to pass them all through. The application env wins over a secret when the key is the same. PR previews do not inherit it. If the secret manager cannot be reached during a deploy, the deployment fails and the old container keeps running.
secretSource.askAdmin: Ask an owner/admin to add one in <section></section>.
secretSource.syncAll: Sync all secrets to the container
secretSource.keysShown: {count, plural, one {# key} other {# keys}} (names only, values are not shown):

maintenance.title: Maintenance mode
maintenance.description: Shows a maintenance page with HTTP 503 on every domain of this application. The container keeps running; only the routing changes.
maintenance.placeholder: We are performing scheduled maintenance. Please check back shortly.
maintenance.messageHint: Plain text, up to {max} characters. Leave it empty for the default message.
maintenance.remote: Not available for applications on a remote server yet.
maintenance.scope: Preview deployments and direct access through the host port are not affected.

active.title: Under maintenance
active.body: Visitors see a 503 page while maintenance mode is on.

webhook.title: Auto-deploy webhook
webhook.description: Every push to the {branch} branch triggers a deploy. Pushes to other branches are ignored; if a deploy is already running, the event is skipped.
webhook.urlCopyFailed: Could not copy the webhook URL

steps.github:
GitHub:

SettingsWebhooksAdd webhook. Payload URL = the URL above, Content type application/json, event Just the push event{hasSecret, select, true {, Secret = the secret below} other {}}.
steps.gitlab:
GitLab:

SettingsWebhooks. URL = the URL above, trigger Push events{hasSecret, select, true {, Secret token = the secret below} other {}}.
steps.reachable: Make sure this API can be reached from the internet (PUBLIC_API_URL).

secret.title: Secret (signature)
secret.activeNote: Active — requests without a matching X-Hub-Signature-256 / X-Gitlab-Token are rejected (401).
secret.inactiveNote: Inactive — anyone who knows the URL can trigger a deploy.

webhook.regenerateNote: The old URL stops working immediately.

previews.title: Pull request previews
previews.descriptionEnabled: Every open PR is built from its branch and run in its own container; it is removed automatically when the PR is closed.
previews.descriptionDisabled: Disabled — enable it in the Settings tab. The provider webhook must send pull request events.

console.note: This shell is inside the container. File changes are lost on redeploy, except in a volume mount.

origin.title: The console cannot be used from this address
origin.body: This panel already has a custom domain ({webOrigin}), and the Console only accepts connections from that domain — not from {browserOrigin}, which you are using now. This is a built-in security protection, not a bug.

volumeBackups.title: Volume backups
volumeBackups.description: A tar.gz archive of each volume in aoox_backups{copied}. Restore stops the container briefly and overwrites the volume contents.

schedule.title: Volume backup schedule
schedule.description: Applies to all volumes of this application. Old scheduled backups beyond the number kept are deleted (per volume).

restoreDialog.title: Restore volume?
restoreDialog.description: The contents of volume {volume} will be deleted and replaced with {file}. The container is stopped during the process. This cannot be undone.

dangerZone.title: Danger zone
dangerZone.deleteDescription: Removes the application with its container, domains, jobs, previews and deployment history. This cannot be undone.

exposedPort.single: This image listens on port {exposed} (EXPOSE), but Container port is {port}. Requests through a domain will fail with Bad Gateway unless the app really listens on {port}.
exposedPort.multiple: This image exposes ports {exposed} (EXPOSE), but Container port is {port}. Requests through a domain will fail with Bad Gateway unless the app really listens on {port}.
exposedPort.applied: Container port set to {port}. The container is being recreated.
